newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Old Mutual Unit Trusts in asset swap.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Old Mutual Unit Trusts in asset swap.

text.p: Old Mutual Unit Trusts, a division of South African life insurer Old Mutual, announced on Thursday it had negotiated a 200 million rand swap agreement with an unidentified foreign institution.

Managing director Selwyn Feldman said the deal, one of the largest ever by a unit trust fund, was negotiated by Old Mutual Investors' Fund and represented about three percent of total assets of 5.9 billion rand.
This was well under the 10 percent foreign exposure limit imposed on institutions by the Reserve Bank.

Investors' Fund portfolio manager Jeremy Bolton said the counterparty had imposed a confidentiality rule which precluded any identification. He said it was possible that Old Mutual would do further business with the same counterparty in future.
Old Mutual International Asset Managers U.K. would handle the investment of the 200 million rand realised by the deal.
"We will go straight into equities, global blue chips. We've given them a mandate saying don't invest in what we can get here. Go for world class companies we can't invest in here," he said.
Bolton welcomed the deal as a risk diversification both geographically and in terms of industry.
The only other Old Mutual fund to have invested abroad is the Global Equity Fund which has taken up its 10 percent allowance on an asset base of 350 million rand.
Physical transfer of the deal would be completed in two weeks.
On June 14 this year, South Africa relaxed foreign exchange controls on domestic institutions by raising the limit on asset swaps to 10 percent of total assets from five percent previously.
Feldman said that without foreign exchange controls, Old Mutual would have wished to take its exposure to 15 percent for the Investors' Fund and would look for further opportunities.
He said the Investors' Fund would remain a domestic fund with the bulk of cash flow invested in South African shares.
Feldman added that Old Mutual would probably seek to exploit the 10 pct foreign exposure limit in most or all of its unit trust products.
